items.item: That path compression is additive to rank, not a competing rule
The amortized-vs-worst-case distinction for a single call under O(α(n))
That a matching lower bound exists for any pointer-based structure, so no cleverer pointer structure beats O(α(m,n)) amortized
Union-find's one structural limit: no Split, so a wrong merge cannot be undone
Path halving and splitting as one-pass alternatives to two-pass compression (out of scope for an exact shared-bound citation; named from their standard definition only, per FACT-CHECK.md)

Union-find's three real uses require the structure to already have the right inputs (a sorted edge order for Kruskal, an edge stream for components, a match decision already made for entity resolution) — it is the cheapest common building block, not the whole algorithm
The timing lab (naive vs. rank vs. rank+compression) as the way this bound becomes a felt difference rather than an asymptotic abstraction
